chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the mortgage (rahn), so he (peace be upon him) said: If the mortgage is greater than the wealth of the debtor, and it is destroyed, he must pay the excess to the owner of the mortgage; and if it is less than his wealth, and the mortgage is destroyed, the owner returns to him the excess of his wealth; and if the mortgage is equal, there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الرَّهْن: Mortgage or pledge (asset held as security for a debt)
key_terms.الْفَضْلَ: The excess (amount by which one value exceeds another)
key_terms.مَالِ الْمُرْتَهِنِ: The wealth/debt of the debtor (one who borrows)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for compensation if a pledged mortgage asset is destroyed in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of risk in *rahn* (mortgage) by establishing that the debtor bears the loss if the collateral's value exceeds the debt, while the creditor absorbs the deficit if the collateral is insufficient, reflecting the principle of equitable risk-sharing. This ruling, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring neither party is unjustly enriched or burdened by the destruction of the pledged asset.
